//: Secrets (connection string, JWT key, admin password) are supplied by user-secrets in development and environment variables in production. See backend/README.md.

Swagger.//RequireAuthentication: Outside Development the UI and JSON need HTTP Basic credentials. Set Swagger:Username and Swagger:Password (env vars or user-secrets). With no credentials configured the endpoint returns 404 rather than publishing the API contract. Set this to false only if the contract is meant to be public.
Swagger.//Servers: Public base URLs advertised in the document. Required behind a reverse proxy so 'Try it out' targets the right host. Leave empty to use the request's own host.

Scraper.//: The scraper runs inside this API — there is no separate worker process. GoogleApiKey is a secret: set Scraper__GoogleApiKey as an environment variable or via user-secrets. Leave it empty to run on OpenStreetMap, which needs no key.
Scraper.//Concurrency: Jobs claimed and run at once, across every kind (search, LinkedIn enrichment, LinkedIn people search all share one queue) — with 1, a second and third queued job of a different kind sit idle behind whichever one a lone worker slot picked up first, even though nothing about them actually conflicts. 4 covers today's three job kinds plus one spare. This process also serves HTTP, so raise it only on an instance sized for it.
Scraper.//LeaseSeconds: How long a claim holds without a heartbeat. Shorter recovers faster after an app-pool recycle; longer tolerates a slow task.
Scraper.//RespectRobotsTxt: Leave on unless you own the sites being crawled.
Scraper.//CrawlerContactEmail: Advertised in the crawler's User-Agent so site owners can reach you.
Scraper.//PlaywrightBrowsersPath: Keep this short — Chromium's own nested install path can exceed Windows' 260-character path limit. See the doc comment on ScraperOptions.PlaywrightBrowsersPath.
Scraper.//PlaywrightConcurrency: Browser CONTEXTS (isolated profiles on one shared Chromium process), not browser instances — tens of MB each, not the 300-500MB a full instance costs. Must exceed Concurrency, since a browser search holds its context for that whole search; set below that and surplus jobs get claimed then block waiting for a context, which looks exactly like a stuck queue. 12 leaves room for Concurrency (4) plus parallel enrichment lanes.
